summary: Romania introduced two-way Contracts for Difference with auctions for 2 GW in 2024 and 3 GW in 2025, and passed a law for Black Sea offshore wind. There are no foreign exchange restrictions, and EU recovery funds back new solar, wind and storage.

access.reason: The Contract for Difference scheme opened with a 2 GW auction in 2024 and a planned 3 GW auction in 2025, split between onshore wind and solar.

terms.reason: Generators receive or pay the difference between a strike price and the market reference price under a two-way contract.

ownership.reason: Romania has no foreign exchange restrictions and a fully liberalised capital account.

build.reason: The transmission operator has announced grid modernisation and a new interconnector to Hungary due in 2029, which shows current limits.

stability.reason: Targets are backed by a national strategy, EU funds and an offshore wind law, and no retroactive cut was found in the period reviewed.

direction.reason: The Contract for Difference auctions and offshore wind law open new routes to market.

stability.reason: No retroactive change was found in the period reviewed.

direction.reason: No change for C&I buyers was found in the sources reviewed.

events.title: First Contract for Difference auction for 2 GW of onshore wind and solar
Offshore wind law sets the framework for Black Sea projects
Second Contract for Difference round planned for 3 GW

sources.title: Romania Country Commercial Guide, trade financing

gaps: Corporate buying routes, buyer credit and connection times were not covered by the sources reviewed, so C&I is not reviewed. Earlier changes to green certificate support were not covered either.
